identity.name: Mike Joyce
identity.summary: The Smiths' drummer, 1982 to 1987: a Manchester punk drummer (the Hoax, Belfast's Victim) who took up the drums after seeing Buzzcocks' John Maher and found in the Smiths a band where he had to drive Johnny Marr's guitars without crowding them. Eighths or two-handed sixteenths on the hat, the snare square on 2 and 4, the bass drum pushing the offbeats, short snare runs into the next phrase, almost no ghost notes: This Charming Man's Motown beat, How Soon Is Now?'s seven-minute groove, The Queen Is Dead's floor tom. 'A great drum fill is only great if it sounds right within the song.' Later with Sinéad O'Connor, Morrissey, Suede, Buzzcocks, PiL and Julian Cope; a broadcaster; his memoir The Drums came out in 2025.

traditions.impact: Buzzcocks' John Maher, whom he saw at fourteen or fifteen: 'that was it'.
Charlie Watts: 'every Stones track that has ever been just sounds fantastic'.

formative_events.event: Saw Buzzcocks in Manchester, 'completely transfixed by John Maher', and pressed his mother for a drum kit.
Joined the Smiths after auditions, in place of Simon Wolstencroft, who had drummed on the demos but would not join.
This Charming Man: his kit sampled and triggered from John Porter's Linn LM-1.
The Queen Is Dead: the intro a loop of his toms on Stephen Street's sampler, played live by hand.

genres.name: Indie rock

genres.name: Punk
genres.notes: The Hoax and Victim before the Smiths; Buzzcocks in the 1990s.

evidence.note: Not measured; a punk drummer by training.

swing.notes: Straight: every transcription is even eighths and sixteenths.

dynamics.balance: The snare and the hat on top; the bass drum busy underneath.

feel_profile.interaction: With Andy Rourke's bass: 'I don't really sit on a groove with a lot of them', since Marr's songs change chords so often; the fills kept to what the song needs.

hand_techniques.name: Two hands on the hat
hand_techniques.description: Sixteenths on the hi-hat with both hands, the snare hand leaving it on 2 and 4 (How Soon Is Now?, Bigmouth Strikes Again).

hand_techniques.name: The floor tom as the time
hand_techniques.description: Eighths on the floor tom in place of the hat (The Queen Is Dead).

hand_techniques.name: Snare runs into the phrase
hand_techniques.description: Sixteenths on the snare from the "and" of 3 or on 4 into the next section.

foot_techniques.name: A busy bass drum
foot_techniques.description: The bass drum on the offbeat sixteenths under a plain backbeat.

coordination.notes: Steady hat or floor-tom ostinatos under a plain backbeat.

voice_language.hihat: Eighths, quarters, or both hands in sixteenths; opened on the "a" of 4.
voice_language.snare: Square on 2 and 4; runs of sixteenths into the next phrase; no ghost notes.
voice_language.kick: On the offbeat eighths and sixteenths under the backbeat.
voice_language.toms: The floor tom as the time on The Queen Is Dead; little else.
voice_language.cymbals: A crash or a splash at the top of four bars.

aesthetic: room on The Queen Is Dead

sample_hints.indie-rock: A 1960s-style kit, bright snare, ringing toms (1983-84); bigger and roomier for The Queen Is Dead.

evidence.note: From the records, not his account.

signature_traits.label: Two hands on the hat
signature_traits.description: Sixteenths on the hi-hat with both hands, broken for the snare on 2 and 4, over a busy bass drum.

signature_traits.label: The floor tom as the time
signature_traits.description: The Queen Is Dead's eighths on the floor tom under the snare.

signature_traits.label: Fills only where the song wants them
signature_traits.description: 'A great drum fill is only great if it sounds right within the song'; short snare runs into the next phrase rather than tom fills.

patterns.name: This Charming Man: the snare on every "and"
patterns.function: Eighths on the hat, the snare on every "and", the bass drum on 1, 2, the "a" of 2 and the "and" of 3: a Motown beat counted in quarters at 104.

evidence.note: Two human tabs agree; the record is his kit sampled and triggered from a Linn LM-1.

patterns.name: How Soon Is Now?: two hands on the hat
patterns.function: Sixteenths on the hat with both hands, leaving it for the snare on 2 and 4; the bass drum on 1, the "a" of 1, the "and" of 2, the "and" of 3 and the "and" of 4. One groove for nearly seven minutes.

patterns.name: What Difference Does It Make?: quarters
patterns.function: Quarters on the hat, the bass drum on 1 and 3, the snare on 2 and 4, a crash at the top of four bars.

patterns.name: Barbarism Begins at Home: funk in eighths
patterns.function: Eighths on the hat, lifted on the "a" of 4 and closed by the foot, the bass drum on 1, the "and" of 2 and 3, the snare on 2 and 4.

patterns.name: The Queen Is Dead: eighths on the floor tom
patterns.function: Eighths on the floor tom in place of the hat, the snare on 2 and 4, the bass drum on 1, the "a" of 1, the "and" of 2, the "and" of 3 and its "a".

patterns.name: Bigmouth Strikes Again: the run into the verse
patterns.function: Two hands on the hat in sixteenths, then the snare in sixteenths from the "and" of 3 into the next verse.

patterns.name: There Is a Light That Never Goes Out: the turn on the snare
patterns.function: Two bars on the snare under eighths on the hat, on 1, 2, the "and" of 3 and 4, then on every beat but 3: the figure that opens the song and leads into each chorus.

A Certain Ratio's drummer, among 'Manchester's finest'.

philosophy.idea: Listen to the music first; a fill is only good if it sounds right in the song, and most drummers are too flamboyant for their own good.

innovations: The Queen Is Dead's sampled tom loop, played by hand on stage
Two-handed sixteenths on the hat under jangling guitars (How Soon Is Now?)
common_misconceptions: That This Charming Man's drums are simply played: Porter's Linn LM-1 triggered samples of Joyce's kit; and that the Smiths' rhythm section were session players, which the 1996 judgment rejected for royalties.

beatbreaker.default_kit_sound: A bright 1960s-style kit, ringing toms (SM Drums' Ludwig); bigger rooms for The Queen Is Dead
generation_rules: Eighths on the hat, or both hands in sixteenths leaving the hat for the snare.
The snare square on 2 and 4; the bass drum on the offbeats.
Fills: short snare runs into the next phrase; a crash or splash on the 1 of four bars.
Straight, no swing, no ghost notes.

lineage_display.lineage_blurb: Buzzcocks' John Maher made him a drummer; the Smiths made him a groove player.
